reviewed_ideas.decision: Retain one combined small-table comb hypothesis as deferred; no established substantial gain and no candidate change.
corrections: PR60 has16 signed windows of2MiB each, totaling32MiB, not16x64KB. The wide variant is interleaved, not planar.
A comb still needs a runtime-base-dependent table. Smaller tables may reduce traffic but do not guarantee zero DRAM accesses or residency. Divergent CUDA constant accesses may serialize.

The two suggestions overlap: retain one geometry family, not two independent improvements. The default11x6 comb gives44 lookup terms and3 doublings; the actual implementation seeds the first term and adds a final offset. This arithmetic increase is substantial versus16 or10 terms.
The arXiv abstract supports author ElGamal/NS3 claims, not grinding performance, GPU transfer or a checked fixed-base comparison table. Full paper and code have not been validated.
The external README memory claims are author hypotheses on a different workload. Do not treat them as measurements of our32MiB or16GiB pipeline.
reviewed_ideas.revisit_when: A concrete parameterization and full arithmetic/traffic model improves the tradeoff or new relevant GPU evidence appears.

reviewed_ideas.decision: First is duplicate of completed experiment; second deferred absent a new concrete bottleneck/removal. No new implementation selected.
corrections: Address-only distance1 rolling L2 prefetch is exactly the already-tested implementation, not a refinement/new proposal.
Zero spills do not prove why allocation improved or that any stalls were removed. ptxas cannot report Stall Long Scoreboard relief; that requires actual GPU profiling.
No proof that this is the only affordable latency-hiding strategy. Divergent addresses do not imply universal serialization; distinguish address spaces and hardware behavior.

Required accumulator/deferred-anchor recurrence cannot simply be discarded. Shared spilling adds traffic and can reduce occupancy; generic RegDem results are not a new end-to-end gain for our now-zero-spill variant.
